s1.syndrome_frame: Palpitations and syncope in a patient with complex congenital heart disease
salient_findings: Tachycardia with heart rate of 183 beats per minute
Irregularly irregular tachycardia with grouped beating on ECG
key_facts: Patient has complex congenital heart disease
Patient has D-transposition of the great arteries
Patient has single ventricle physiology
Patient has a large ventricular septal defect with outflow extension
Patient has Fontan circulation
Patient was prescribed diltiazem and apixaban
Patient experienced persistent tachycardia and palpitations
ECG showed irregularly irregular tachycardia with grouped beating
Transesophageal echocardiogram showed no intracardiac thrombus
ECG after diltiazem administration showed regular narrow complex tachycardia
ECG with adenosine showed temporary heart block with continuation of supraventricular tachycardia

raw.champion: Intra-atrial reentrant tachycardia (IART) with variable atrioventricular block
raw.rationale: The patient's ECG shows irregularly irregular tachycardia with grouped beating and intermittently visible P waves, which is consistent with IART. The use of diltiazem and adenosine also supports this diagnosis, as IART can be sensitive to these medications. Additionally, the patient's complex congenital heart disease and Fontan circulation increase the risk for IART.

rejected.label: Atrial Tachycardia with variable block
rejected.why: While atrial tachycardia can present with similar ECG findings, the patient's response to diltiazem and adenosine, as well as the presence of grouped beating, makes IART a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Ectopic Atrial Tachycardia
rejected.why: Ectopic atrial tachycardia typically presents with a more regular rhythm and may not respond to diltiazem and adenosine in the same way as IART.

rejected.label: Atrial Flutter with variable conduction
rejected.why: Atrial flutter typically presents with a more regular rhythm and a characteristic sawtooth pattern on ECG, which is not seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Supraventricular tachycardia with aberrancy
rejected.why: While supraventricular tachycardia can present with a wide complex tachycardia, the patient's ECG shows a narrow complex tachycardia, making this diagnosis less likely.
